slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 14:18: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High—
slides.body: “Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High—”
slides.heading: Gen 14:18

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the claim based on Melchizedek's name and title.
slides.body: Hebrews interprets Melchizedek as ‘king of righteousness’ and king of Salem as ‘king of peace’—qualities Christians associate with Jesus.
slides.heading: Did these royal titles predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents Hebrews's explicit christological use of Melchizedek's titles.
slides.body: Hebrews itself highlights the symbolism while comparing Melchizedek with the Son of God. King, priest, righteousness and peace form a coherent portrait within its larger argument about Jesus.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three distinguishes Hebrews's typology from a prediction in Genesis.
slides.body: Genesis applies the name and place-title to Melchizedek himself. It says nothing about a future bearer. Hebrews openly reads those features typologically in relation to Christ—a genuine NT connection, but not a verbal forecast in Genesis.
slides.heading: Interpretation, not prediction

title: Did ‘king of righteousness and peace’ predict Jesus?
